title: Sports & Olympic Records
description: 36 original questions on Olympic history, football, tennis, athletics, rules, and all-time sporting records.
author: QuizRooms

questions.prompt: Which swimmer holds the all-time Olympic record with 28 medals (including 23 golds)?
questions.explanation: Phelps won 8 gold medals at the 2008 Beijing Olympics alone.

questions.prompt: Who holds the men's 100-meter sprint world record of 9.58 seconds?
questions.explanation: Jamaican sprinter Usain Bolt set the 9.58s record in Berlin in 2009.

questions.prompt: In which city were the first modern Olympic Games held in 1896?
questions.explanation: 241 athletes from 14 nations competed in Athens in April 1896.

questions.prompt: How many players from one team are on the field at the start of a regulation football (soccer) match?
questions.explanation: Each team fields 10 outfield players plus 1 goalkeeper.

questions.prompt: What is the official distance of a standard Olympic marathon?
questions.explanation: The exact 42.195 km (26 miles 385 yards) distance was standardized from the 1908 London Games.

questions.prompt: What are the five colors of the Olympic rings?
choices: Blue, yellow, black, green, and red
Blue, white, black, green, and red
Orange, yellow, black, green, and red
Blue, yellow, purple, green, and red
questions.answer: Blue, yellow, black, green, and red
questions.explanation: At least one of these five colors (plus the white background) appeared on every national flag in 1913.

questions.prompt: Which tennis player has won the most men's Grand Slam singles titles (24)?
questions.explanation: Djokovic captured his 24th Grand Slam title at the 2023 US Open.

questions.prompt: Which tennis Grand Slam tournament is played on grass courts in London?
questions.explanation: Founded in 1877, Wimbledon is the oldest tennis tournament in the world.

questions.prompt: How many points is a shot made from behind the arc worth in standard basketball?
questions.explanation: The 3-point line was adopted by the NBA in 1979 and FIBA in 1984.

questions.prompt: How high is a standard basketball hoop rim above the court floor?
questions.explanation: James Naismith nailed the first peach baskets to a 10-foot gymnasium balcony in 1891.

questions.prompt: Which country hosted the 2024 Summer Olympic Games?
questions.explanation: Paris hosted the Summer Olympics for the third time (1900, 1924, 2024).

questions.prompt: Which city is scheduled to host the 2028 Summer Olympic Games?
questions.explanation: Los Angeles will become the third city (after London and Paris) to host three Summer Olympics.

questions.prompt: In boxing, what is the maximum number of rounds in a standard men's world championship bout?
questions.explanation: Championship bouts were reduced from 15 to 12 rounds in the 1980s for fighter safety.

questions.prompt: Which country won the most gold medals in the history of the Summer Olympics?
questions.explanation: The US leads the all-time Summer Olympics medal table with over 1,000 gold medals.

questions.prompt: In volleyball, how many players per team are on the court at one time?
questions.explanation: Teams rotate clockwise each time they win back the serve.

questions.prompt: Which Formula 1 drivers are tied for the most World Drivers' Championships (7 each)?
choices: Juan Manuel Fangio and Niki Lauda
questions.explanation: Both Schumacher and Hamilton have won seven F1 world titles.

questions.prompt: In golf, what is a score of two strokes under par on a single hole called?
questions.explanation: One under par is a birdie, two under is an eagle, and three under is an albatross.

questions.prompt: Which country invented the modern game of badminton (formalized in England from a game played in Pune)?
questions.explanation: British officers in Pune (Poona), India, brought the game back to Badminton House in Gloucestershire.

questions.prompt: Which gymnastics legend won the Olympic women's all-around gold medal in both 2016 and 2024?
questions.explanation: Biles is the most decorated gymnast in World Championship and US Olympic history.

questions.prompt: Who became the first gymnast to score a perfect 10.0 at the Olympic Games (Montreal 1976)?
questions.explanation: The scoreboard couldn't display 10.00 and famously showed '1.00' instead.

questions.prompt: What is the regulation length of an Olympic-size swimming pool?
questions.explanation: Olympic pools are 50 meters long, 25 meters wide, and have 10 lanes (8 used in finals).

questions.prompt: In tennis, what score does 'deuce' represent?
questions.explanation: From deuce, a player must win two consecutive points to take the game.

questions.prompt: Which African country has dominated Olympic men's 3,000m steeplechase and marathon running, producing Eliud Kipchoge?
questions.explanation: Kipchoge won back-to-back Olympic marathon golds in 2016 and 2020.

questions.prompt: Which Moroccan middle-distance runner still holds the men's 1,500m world record (3:26.00) and won double gold at Athens 2004?
questions.explanation: El Guerrouj won both the 1,500m and 5,000m golds at the 2004 Olympics.

questions.prompt: Which club has won the most UEFA Champions League titles (15 as of 2024)?
questions.explanation: Real Madrid won the inaugural 1956 European Cup and claimed their 15th in 2024.

questions.prompt: In chess, which piece can jump over other pieces and moves in an L-shape?
questions.explanation: The knight moves two squares in one direction and one square perpendicular.

questions.prompt: What is the highest possible break in a single frame of snooker (without free balls)?
questions.explanation: A 147 maximum break requires potting all 15 reds with 15 blacks followed by all 6 colors.

questions.prompt: Which Swedish pole vaulter repeatedly broke the world record and won Olympic gold in Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024?
questions.explanation: Mondo Duplantis cleared 6.25m in Paris to break his own world record.

questions.prompt: Which sport made its Olympic debut at the 2024 Paris Summer Games?
questions.explanation: Breaking (breakdancing) debuted in Paris 2024, while skateboarding and surfing debuted in Tokyo 2020.

questions.prompt: How many innings are in a standard regulation baseball game?
questions.explanation: Extra innings are played if the score is tied after nine innings.

questions.prompt: In football (soccer), how far from the goal line is the penalty spot placed?
questions.explanation: The penalty mark sits 11 meters (12 yards) directly in front of the center of the goal.

questions.prompt: Which Jamaican sprinter holds the women's 100m Olympic record (10.61s) and won back-to-back 100m/200m Olympic doubles?
questions.explanation: Thompson-Herah won both the 100m and 200m in Rio 2016 and Tokyo 2020.

questions.prompt: Which ancient Greek festival held every four years in Olympia inspired the modern Olympic Games?
questions.explanation: First recorded in 776 BC, the ancient Games enforced an Olympic Truce across Greek city-states.

questions.prompt: Which cycling race is the most prestigious annual three-week Grand Tour, ending traditionally in Paris?
questions.explanation: The race leader wears the iconic yellow jersey (maillot jaune).

questions.prompt: Which Egyptian football star became the first African player to win three Premier League Golden Boots?
questions.explanation: Mohamed Salah won Golden Boots in 2017–18, 2018–19, and 2021–22 (plus 2024–25).

questions.prompt: In which sport is the Davis Cup the premier international men's team trophy?
questions.explanation: First contested in 1900, the Davis Cup is billed as the 'World Cup of Tennis'.
